Concealed challenge: concealed injection of out-of-envelope process commands. Rival: counting delayed alarms as normal operation. Physical limitation: stop the bench immediately upon an interlock miss. F160 / Trustworthy Autonomous Neural Nanomanufacturing Platforms At The Limit Primary endpoint: independent quality-release assessor agreement [%]. Concealed challenge: blinded replacement of quality inspectors. Rival: false consensus from shared evaluator software. excluded.title: SWARM METROLOGY AND AUTONOMOUS REPAIR REQUALIFICATION AT THE LIMIT STARLI Research Works | White Rainbow Scientific Library Prospective Research Review Edition | October 2026 A robotic swarm can repair a structure, repeat a successful movement, and agree on a measurement while still misunderstanding the repaired object's physical condition. This monograph explores a deeper engineering question: can distributed measuring agents independently requalify repaired geometry, material properties, and functional capacity when their sensors may share a drifting reference, a common software defect, or an unobservable state? The proposed research programme couples distributed metrology, traceable repair evidence, and independent adjudication. Its mathematical foundation addresses correlated sensor errors, marginalization of calibration bias, measurement observability, covariance intersection, robust estimation, confidence and coverage, sequential decisions, conformity assessment, calibration genealogy, and long-horizon reliability. Thirty distinct mathematical signposts link physical assumptions, measured units, falsifiable predictions, and proposed experiments. Rather than treating sensor consensus as physical truth, the work requires a blind external witness capable of defeating a preferred interpretation. Across 82 research chapters and 410 separately paginated study units, the atlas investigates hidden common-mode calibration faults, coordinate-frame and timestamp drift, non-Gaussian measurement noise, blind regions, firmware contamination, robot-sensor attrition, cross-modal references, release guard bands, and second-laboratory reproducibility. Each chapter specifies measurable quantities, a controlled intervention, a strong conventional comparator, and a research stop condition. Two hundred Research Gates invite future researchers to conduct discriminating experiments under real resource budgets and genuine uncertainty. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos outline revisable concepts that can be corrected, rejected, divided, or rebuilt by successor teams. A separate Excel companion cross-references formulas, chapters, studies, Gates, source DOI metadata, and PDF pages. External references include metrology standards, distributed estimation research, and modular robotics literature; earlier STARLI research works serve only as conceptual genealogy.
